title: Border images (overview)
learningObjectives: Explain border images (overview) and apply the visual effect with a usable fallback.

understand.concept: border-image uses an image or gradient as a source for an element's border. border-image-slice defines how the source is divided, border-image-width controls rendered border thickness, border-image-outset extends it, and border-image-repeat controls edge scaling or tiling.
understand.whyItMatters: Border images are specialised and can be harder to maintain than ordinary borders. Provide a conventional border fallback and test scaling at different sizes.
understand.analogy: A border image is like cutting a frame pattern into corners, edges, and a centre so it can be fitted around a box.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual painting, clipping, and media behaviour follow CSS rendering rules.

explain.narrative: The gradient is sliced and used as the border image. The transparent border declaration reserves a border area.

examples.explanation: The gradient is sliced and used as the border image. The transparent border declaration reserves a border area.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered visual example demonstrating the CSS effect.

practise.guidedTask: Experiment with a gradient border image and compare it with a regular border. Keep a fallback border for browsers or cases where the effect is unavailable.
practise.independentTask: Create a decorative component using this effect. Test readability, responsive sizing, and a baseline appearance when the effect is unavailable.
hints: Keep important information in semantic HTML.
Test the effect on different sizes and backgrounds.
Do not let decorative effects obscure focus or text.

questions.prompt: Which property divides the border image source into regions?
questions.explanation: border-image-slice defines how the source image is divided into border regions.

questions.prompt: What should accompany a decorative CSS effect?
options: Readable content and a usable fallback
Essential information available only in the effect
questions.answer: Readable content and a usable fallback
questions.explanation: Decorative effects should enhance content rather than become the only way to access it.
